note: Conformance vectors for the veyq v1 crypto suite. Bytes are lowercase hex. Most Argon2 vectors use light params (m=8 MiB) for fast conformance; recovery_argon2id_m32768 + auth.auth_keypair deliberately pin the PRODUCTION param (m=32 MiB, t=3 — the value all clients ship in ARGON) to drift-proof the password-derived KEK + the auth keypair and stop the B1-class mismatch (m=65536 vs 32768) recurring. The hybrid KEM is X-Wing, held to its draft's own published vectors (#xwing); its encapsulation is randomized in practice and made deterministic in a vector by eseed.

device_password_argon2id.note: kekDevicePassword (uc.account.trust-device): Argon2id(lp(deviceFactor) || lp(utf8(password)), salt). Factor-first like password_secret_argon2id; the device-bound factor replaces the Secret Key.

recovery_argon2id_m32768.note: kekRecovery at PRODUCTION Argon2 params (m=32 MiB) — pins the recovery KEK at the params every client ships, so the B1-class param mismatch (m=65536 vs 32768) cannot silently recur. Same inputs as recovery_argon2id, only m differs.

auth_salt.note: deriveAuthSalt (ADR 0003): HKDF-SHA256(ikm=utf8(email.trim().toLowerCase()), salt=instance_salt, info="veyq/v1/auth-salt", 16). email_utf8 is the raw pre-normalization input the impl normalizes. Asserted on web; the operator-blind backend only VERIFIES signatures, so it does not derive this.

auth_keypair.note: deriveAuthKeypair (ADR 0003): seed=Argon2id(utf8(password), auth_salt, PRODUCTION params m=32768); private_key=seed, public_key=Ed25519.getPublicKey(seed). Pins the password->Ed25519 auth identity byte-for-byte, so a refactor cannot silently move it (it was only a non-vector sign/verify round-trip before). auth_salt is auth.auth_salt.auth_salt.

xwing.note: The suite's hybrid KEM is X-Wing (ADR 0017 decision 2), held to draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-11 Appendix C: these three vectors are copied verbatim from that revision (fetched from https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-11.txt), not produced by this suite, so this group is a cross-implementation anchor rather than a regression pin. The draft heads its Appendix C as provisional ("TODO: replace with test vectors that re-use ML-KEM, X25519 values"); a later revision that changes them is a deliberate update of this group, never a silent one. seed is the 32-byte decapsulation key (sk = seed); pk = pk_M || pk_X (1216 bytes) is GenerateKeyPairDerand(seed); eseed (64 bytes: ML-KEM encapsulation coins || X25519 ephemeral secret) makes EncapsulateDerand(pk, eseed) deterministic, giving ct = ct_M || ct_X (1120 bytes) and the 32-byte shared secret ss; Decapsulate(ct, sk) gives ss back.

seal.note: ADR 0072: one vector per seal PURPOSE, keyed by it — a live purpose earns a vector and a vector with no live purpose is deleted; the TS conformance test compares these keys with the typed union (SEAL_PURPOSES / SEAL_TO_PURPOSES) in both directions. A seal binds its purpose AND the object it is stored as. context_bytes = lp(utf8(purpose)) || lp(field)… in the purpose's fixed field order, where lp = u32be(len) || bytes, an id field is the UTF-8 of its canonical lowercase UUID (a share id: of its 43-character base64url bearer token, which a share keeps because it is a capability), an epoch/version is u64be, and a blob role is its UTF-8 name: an open, bounded token ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,15}$ (the contract's NodeKind token), so a new role is a new value, not a field change, and the bytes of every existing role stay as they are; a role together with ownerId (the owning object: a media, or a node for a cover or a file's content) is what binds a blob key wrap to its application and kind (ADR 0079 §9). Memories' roles are ORIGINAL/THUMBNAIL/PREVIEW/COVER, Files' is FILE_CONTENT (#file_blob). blob-meta is a blob's sealed metadata under that blob's own K_blob (its kek here is #file_blob's blob key): purpose only, because the key is the binding, as for the blob's chunk frames, and its AAD (0x02 || 'v1' || lp('blob-meta'), 16 bytes) can never equal a frame's 8-byte u32be(index) || u32be(total). Its plaintext is compact UTF-8 JSON {v, type, name?, modifiedAt?, sha256?} in that key order (name NFC; sha256 the plaintext's SHA-256 as 43 base64url characters, written where the blob is a person's file as it is), padded with spaces (0x20) to the next multiple of 256 bytes, at most 1024. sym: blob = 0x02 || nonce(12) || AES-256-GCM(kek, nonce, plaintext, aad) with aad = 0x02 || utf8('v1') || context_bytes. asym (to an X-Wing encapsulation key, #xwing): blob = 0x01 || ct(1120) || nonce(12) || AES-256-GCM(HKDF-SHA256(ss, salt='', info=utf8('veyq/v1/wrap') || context_bytes, 32), nonce, plaintext, aad) with aad = 0x01 || utf8('v1') || context_bytes, where ct = ct_M || ct_X and ss are X-Wing's; pk and eseed are #xwing vector 0's, so ct is that vector's ct and the recipient's decapsulation key is its sk. A purpose with an empty context binds its purpose only, because its key is unique to one object (ADR 0072 Decision 2). The sym blobs and every context_bytes were generated by an independent Python implementation of this encoding. The asym blobs were generated by an independent node:crypto (OpenSSL) implementation of the wrap layer over #xwing vector 0's published ct and ss. moderation-grant's blob (ADR 0099 § 2: the instance moderation key M_n sealed to a moderator's identity, [epoch]) was generated the same way by an independent Python implementation (cryptography/OpenSSL AES-GCM and HKDF) over the same ct and ss. report-share, report-link and moderation-report (ADR 0093 §§ 1-2: a report share's keys under the report's fresh K_report, addressed by the item, and the report's sealed part to the epoch's public half) were generated the same way by an independent Python implementation (cryptography/OpenSSL), their plaintexts by the same implementation of #report_bundle's encodings. moderation-report-contact (ADR 0093 § 11: the reporter's contact, sealed apart from the report's body to the same epoch's public half so it can go alone, [epoch]) and moderation-report's body without the contact were regenerated the same way by an independent Python implementation (cryptography/OpenSSL), which first re-derived the earlier moderation-report blob byte for byte. moderation-objection (ADR 0093 § 7: an affected member's objection sealed to the epoch's public half, [epoch, statementId]), its plaintext the note's encoding, was generated the same way by an independent Python implementation (cryptography/OpenSSL), which first re-derived moderation-note's blob byte for byte. moderation-statement-facts (sym; ADR 0093 § 7: a moderator's facts of a statement of reasons, sealed once under the statement's fresh 32-byte K_facts — its kek here —, bound to the case and the statement id the moderator's browser mints, [caseId, statementId]; its plaintext the note's encoding) and moderation-facts-key (asym: that K_facts — its plaintext, the sym vector's kek — wrapped to one affected member's identity, [caseId, statementId, accountId]) were generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography/OpenSSL) written from this note, which first re-derived the retired per-member moderation-facts blob, moderation-note's blob and report-share's blob byte for byte. moderation-order (ADR 0093 § 12: an authority's reference sealed to the epoch's public half by the client that enters the order, bound to the order id that client mints, [epoch, orderId]; its plaintext the note's encoding) was generated the same way by an independent Python implementation (cryptography/OpenSSL), which first re-derived moderation-objection's blob byte for byte. moderation-step-facts (ADR 0093 § 7: the facts of a Server Owner's own step over content — a member's sign-in block, a tenant taken offline — sealed to the epoch's public half by admin-web or veyq-admin for the log, bound to the statement id that client mints, [epoch, statementId]; its plaintext the note's encoding) was generated the same way by an independent Python implementation (cryptography/OpenSSL), which first re-derived moderation-order's blob byte for byte. moderation-note (ADR 0093 § 11, ADR 0099 § 6: a moderator's free text, a decision's note or an extension's reason, sealed to the epoch's public half and bound to its case, [epoch, caseId]; its plaintext is lp(utf8(text)) zero-padded to the next multiple of 512 bytes) was generated the same way by an independent Python implementation (cryptography/OpenSSL). identity-pin (ADR 0104: one pin of the identity-pin store, sealed under the Master Key and bound to its pinId, a 32-byte digest field encoded as its raw bytes; its plaintext is #identity_pin's entry) and identity-pins' version-2 head plaintext (#identity_pin's head of the empty set) were generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography/OpenSSL AES-GCM and HKDF, hashlib/hmac), which first re-derived identity-pins' and device-register's earlier blobs, item_mark_self's tags and fingerprint's digits byte for byte. item-favorites' plaintext is #item_mark_self's binary encoding (tag || 16-byte ids, inbox #500); its blob was regenerated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography/OpenSSL AES-GCM), which first re-derived the earlier JSON-plaintext blob byte for byte. expense-entry-key is an Expenses revision's own random K_rev wrapped under its Pot's K_node (kek here), bound to (scope, Pot node, entry, revision) — the shape of a K_blob under its owner (ADR 0108 decision 4); its plaintext is #field_seal['expense-entry']'s parent_key, so a re-key rewrites this wrap and no body.

field_seal.note: ADR 0093 § 9: one vector per FIELD purpose, keyed by it; the TS conformance test compares these keys with FIELD_PURPOSES in both directions, and no purpose is in two of seal.sym, seal.asym and field_seal. A field seals one revision of a text or icon field under a key of its own, derived per write from the key it would otherwise be sealed under (parent_key): field_key = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=parent_key, salt, info=utf8('veyq/v1/field/' || purpose), 32), with a 16-byte salt drawn fresh per write. envelope = 0x03 || salt(16) || nonce(12) || AES-256-GCM(field_key, nonce, plaintext, aad) with aad = 0x03 || utf8('v1') || context_bytes; context_bytes as in #seal. The salt is not in the AAD: another salt derives another key. So field_key opens this one envelope and nothing else under parent_key, and reveals nothing about parent_key (HKDF is one-way) - it is the key a report hands over. Each entry keeps the context, parent key (the kek), nonce and plaintext its purpose's plain-seal vector carried before ADR 0093 § 9 moved it here. Generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography HKDF/AESGCM). expense-entry (ADR 0108 decision 4) is the one purpose whose parent_key is not a node, share or tenant key but the revision's own random K_rev, which #seal.sym['expense-entry-key'] wraps: a re-key rewraps K_rev and the envelope and its SHA-256 (the digest a later revision's heads name) stay byte-identical. Its plaintext is a revision of contracts/expenses/entry.v1.schema.json as compact UTF-8 JSON padded to the smallest size class that carries it (u32be(len) || bytes || zeros to 512, 2048, 8192 or 16384 bytes) — here 512.

group_name_key.note: cr-0096 (ADR 0027): the GROUP name-key K_name derived from the name's content-epoch key E_e — K_name = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=E_e, salt="" (empty), info=utf8("veyq/v1/group-name-key"), 32). Handing a pending invitee K_name lets them open the SAME canonical encryptedName the members read (closing cr-0094's divergent-name lie). HKDF one-wayness means K_name leaks the name and nothing else — not E_e, not the content key. epoch_key is the 32-byte E_e (0x44*32 here); okm is K_name (the kek of sym_group_name + the plaintext of asym_group_name_key).

space_icon_key.note: uc.spaces.set-space-icon (ADR 0027): the space icon-key K_icon derived from the icon's content-epoch key E_e — K_icon = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=E_e, salt="" (empty), info=utf8("veyq/v1/space-icon-key"), 32). The icon plaintext is padded to a constant length, then sealed under K_icon (symWrap, 'space-icon' AAD context), so every sealedIcon is byte-identical in length — the operator cannot tell a logo from a photo. The info string is DISTINCT from group_name_key (domain separation: an icon-key wrap can never be reinterpreted as a name-key or a scope-grant). HKDF one-wayness means K_icon leaks the icon and nothing else — not E_e, not the content key. epoch_key is the 32-byte E_e (0x44*32 here, shared with group_name_key so only the info differs); okm is K_icon.

slug_token.note: AD-26 blinded slug token: slugKey = HKDF(contentKey, "veyq/v1/slug-token:" + parentSlot); token = HMAC-SHA256(slugKey, NFC(slug)). parentSlot = parent node id, or scope id at the root. (slug stored DECOMPOSED/NFD on purpose, so a platform that skips NFC normalization computes a different token and fails this vector.)

name_folding.note: inbox #350 / ADR 0080 (owner decision): a node's name is folded to a slug BEFORE slug_token HMACs it, by its KIND's function (the web registry's KindDescriptor.slug, default slugify). Containers (folders, Memories, chapters) keep slugify: NFC first (inbox #365), lowercase, ä/ö/ü/ß -> ae/oe/ue/ss (the table sees composed letters only, which the NFC step guarantees), NFKD, U+0300-U+036F dropped, every run outside [a-z0-9] -> one '-', one edge '-' trimmed, and 'n' + base36(FNV-1a-32 over the NFC name's UTF-16 code units) when nothing is left; it is the URL segment and the uniqueness at once. Files use fileNameSlug: NFC, then the locale-free default Unicode lowercasing (JavaScript toLowerCase: context-sensitive final sigma, U+0130 -> i + U+0307), nothing else (punctuation and spaces kept, no trim; the member UI trims before folding). FROZEN INTO TOKENS: every stored slug token is HMAC(slugKey, NFC(fold(name))), so a changed folding stops a stored node from colliding with its own name; any client must reproduce these outputs exactly, and changing one is a stored-format change (ADR 0072). No slug library, for the same reason. slug_token's input 'italien-2026-café' (stored NFD) is no slugify output (slugify strips accents): it pins the token's own NFC step, which a fileNameSlug output does reach. Combining marks and conjoining jamo are written as \u escapes. Generated by an independent Python implementation (unicodedata) and checked against the TS functions (web/src/shared/naming.ts).

directory_entry.note: ADR 0080 Decision 2: a node's directory entry lives under its PARENT's content key; ADR 0093 § 9: as a node-name field, under the field key derived from it per write (#field_seal). The slug token keeps its derivation (slug_token); the node-name field and the content-key seal also bind the placement version the wire stores them at since ADR 0080 Decision 3 (a stored-format change made before the first release, ADR 0072), and this case chains them: the parent is the node of seal.sym['content-key'] (its content key is that vector's plaintext, wrapped under K_SC = its kek), the child's name is a node-name field envelope whose field_key derives from the parent's content key and the envelope's salt, and the child's slug token is keyed by the parent's content key with parentSlot = the parent's node id. The same name derived or slugged under K_SC is what the pre-ADR-0080 client wrote: the child envelope does not open under K_SC, and the K_SC-keyed token differs. Generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography AESGCM/HKDF, hmac).

file_blob.note: cr-files-application P3-S1: a Files blob. The blob role is an open, bounded token (seal.note), so FILE_CONTENT needs no purpose of its own: the blob-key seal with role FILE_CONTENT and ownerId = the file node's id binds the wrap to Files' kind and to its node (ADR 0079 §9), by the same encoding as Memories' roles. The chain: the parent is the node of seal.sym['content-key'] (its content key is that vector's plaintext); the file node's content key is a content-key seal under it (node); the blob key is a blob-key seal under the file node's content key (blobKey). Generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography AESGCM), which first reproduced seal.sym['blob-key'] and seal.sym['content-key'] byte for byte.

share_write_token.note: ADR 0076 share write proof: writeToken = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_share, salt="" (empty), info=utf8("veyq/v1/share-write:" + shareId), 32); the share stores verifier = SHA-256(writeToken), and naming yourself on the link presents writeToken (X-Share-Write). The share id is in the info so a token is bound to its link (ADR 0072): other_share_id under the same K_share gives a different token. The label is its own, so the token opens no seal and reveals nothing about K_share.

chunk_frame.note: Chunked-AEAD frame: nonce(12) || AEAD(contentKey, nonce, plaintext, aad) with aad = u32be(index) || u32be(total). For resumable upload + segmented streaming.

chunk_frame_size.note: The frame size of a blob's chunk_frame sequence (ADR 0013 §3). Every frame but the last carries exactly plaintextBytes of plaintext, sealed to nonceBytes + plaintextBytes + tagBytes; the last carries 1..plaintextBytes, and an empty blob is one frame carrying 0. So a blob's sealed byteSize fixes its chunkCount = ceil(byteSize / (nonceBytes + plaintextBytes + tagBytes)), and a byteSize under nonceBytes + tagBytes, or one whose last frame of several would carry no plaintext, is no frame sequence at all. The backend and every client read the size from here.

dedup_token.note: AD-09 media dedup token: dedupKey = HKDF(contentKey, "veyq/v1/media-dedup"); token = HMAC-SHA256(dedupKey, SHA256(content)).

kdf_params.note: kdfParams wire format: u32be t || m || p || dkLen || salt. The one fixed-layout cross-platform serialization (web encodes at setup/reset, mobile decodes at login) — pins encode + decode round-trip.

fingerprint.note: Identity safety number: sha256("veyq/v1/fingerprint" || lp(kem) || lp(sign)) -> 6 groups of 5 decimal digits, each a 40-bit big-endian hash chunk mod 100000, space-joined. Detects active-operator key-substitution when two users compare out-of-band. Input is fixed synthetic bytes (the fingerprint is a pure byte-hash; key validity is irrelevant). hash is that SHA-256 digest itself (fingerprintHash): the safety-number QR carries it and an identity-pin entry pins it (ADR 0104 decision 3), so the digits render from a stored hash alone (fingerprintDigits). chain_code (ADR 0111 decision 14): the ten digits shown beside the safety number, rendered from a key-chain head (#key_chain's heads) as the first two groups of the same rendering - each a 40-bit big-endian chunk of the head mod 100000. The safety-number QR (veyqid:2) carries the fingerprint hash and the head.

secret_key_proof.note: ADR 0060 Decision 2: the Secret-Key proof key and the four statements it signs (rotation, change-password, recovery, change-email). seed = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = secret_key, salt = empty, info = "veyq/v1/secret-key-proof"), Ed25519 keypair from the seed. Statement = lp(utf8(domain)) || lp(field)..., each field the DECODED bytes of its wire value. wrap digest = sha256(lp(wrappedKey) || lp(kdfParams)). Signatures are Ed25519 (deterministic), so they are pinned too. Asserted by packages/crypto AND by the backend (SecretKeyProofTest). The rotation is the one statement two proof keys sign: the current one (signature) and the new one it registers (possession_signature).

rotation.note: lp(domain) || lp(sha256(currentIdentityPublicKey)) || lp(sha256(identityPublicKey)) || lp(sha256(wrappedIdentityPrivateKey)) || lp(wrapDigest(passwordWrap)) || lp(wrapDigest(recoveryWrap)) || lp(sha256(keyChainStep statement)) || lp(currentAuthPublicKey) || lp(authPublicKey) || lp(secretKeyProofPublicKey) || lp(utf8(stageId)) || lp(stagedGrantsDigest). key_chain_step_statement is #key_chain.links[1].statement, stage_id and staged_grants_digest are #rotation_stage's. signature is the CURRENT proof key's (#secret_key_proof.key), possession_signature the NEW one's, derived from new_secret_key; secret_key_proof_public_key is that new public key.

recovery.note: lp(domain) || lp(sha256(utf8(token))) || lp(authPublicKey) || lp(wrapDigest(passwordWrap)). The token is the wire string itself (not base64-decoded): it is an opaque handle, and its UTF-8 bytes are what both stacks hold.

change_email.note: lp(domain) || lp(currentAuthPublicKey) || lp(authPublicKey) || lp(utf8(normalize(email))). normalize = trim + lower-case (the auth-salt rule, ADR 0003); email_utf8 is the raw input each stack normalizes itself, so the vector pins the normalization too. Generated by an independent Python implementation (hashlib + cryptography Ed25519).

auth_attestation.note: uc.account.change-email: the attestation by the CURRENT auth key that installs a new one under a new address. statement = lp(utf8(domain)) || lp(utf8(userId)) || lp(utf8(normalize(email))) || lp(authPublicKey); signature = Ed25519 under the current auth private key (deterministic, so pinned). normalize = trim + lower-case; email_utf8 is the raw input. A password change's attestation signs the new key's raw bytes alone, so the two can never stand for each other. Generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography Ed25519). Asserted by packages/crypto AND by the backend (EmailChangeAttestationTest).

erase_account.note: uc.account.erase-account (ADR 0101 decision 1): the member's password proof at the self-service door. statement = lp(utf8(domain)) || lp(utf8(userId)) || lp(nonce), nonce = the DECODED bytes of a login challenge the server mints and spends with the request, so no captured proof erases twice; signature = Ed25519 under the account's auth private key (deterministic, so pinned). Generated by the same independent Python implementation. Asserted by packages/crypto AND by the backend (AuthAttestationTest).

item_mark_self.note: ADR 0068 §9: which item-mark entry is the caller's own. k_self = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = master_key, salt = empty, info = "veyq/v1/item-mark-self", 32); marks = SHA-256(lp(utf8(id)) || ...) over the marked ids de-duplicated and sorted ascending (canonical lowercase UUIDs, so code-unit, code-point and byte order agree); statement = lp(utf8("item-mark-self")) || lp(utf8(scopeId)) || lp(utf8(nodeId)) || lp(marks) -- the typed-seal canonical encoding (seal.note), a digest field being its 32 raw bytes; tag = HMAC-SHA256(k_self, statement). The tag rides INSIDE the item-favorites plaintext, which is tag (32 bytes) || each distinct marked id's 16 RFC 4122 bytes in ascending order (inbox #500: 16 bytes a mark instead of a 36-character JSON string) -- each case's plaintext; seal.sym.item-favorites carries case 'one'. Generated by an independent Python implementation (hashlib/hmac + cryptography HKDF); the plaintexts and the new item-favorites blob by an independent Python implementation (uuid, cryptography/OpenSSL AES-GCM) that first re-derived the earlier JSON-plaintext blob and both tags byte for byte. Asserted by packages/crypto only: the server holds no master key.

grant_signature.note: ADR 0028 Decision 6: the grant signature. statement = lp(utf8("grant")) || lp(utf8(scopeId)) || lp(utf8(scopeKind)) || lp(u64be(epoch)) || lp(utf8(recipientUserId)) || lp(sha256(recipient_identity_public_key)) || lp(sha256(wrapped_grant)) -- the typed-seal canonical encoding, both byte strings DECODED from their wire base64. signature = Ed25519(identity signing key, statement), deterministic, so pinned. sign_seed is the identity private signing key (Identity.priv.sign). Generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography Ed25519). Asserted by packages/crypto only: the server stores and relays the signature and never verifies it.

pairing_channel.note: ADR 0059 §11: the pairing channel. The QR carries 32 random bytes `secret`; handle = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = secret, salt = empty, info = "veyq/v1/pairing-handle", 32) is all the server ever receives, and channel_key = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = secret, salt = empty, info = "veyq/v1/pairing-channel", 32) MACs the two values the relay carries. Each statement is the typed-statement canonical encoding (seal.note): lp(utf8(label)) || lp(field)..., where a byte field is bound whole and the code is its six ASCII digits. mac = HMAC-SHA256(channel_key, statement). The two answer labels keep an add-a-device answer from passing for a sign-in one and back. transport_key and envelope are fixed synthetic bytes (the MAC is a pure byte function; key validity is irrelevant). Generated by an independent Python implementation (hashlib/hmac + cryptography HKDF). Asserted by packages/crypto only: the server never receives the secret or the channel key.

moderation_key.note: ADR 0099 § 2: the instance moderation key of one epoch. m is the epoch's 32-byte random M_n; kem_seed = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = m, salt = empty, info = utf8('veyq/v1/moderation/kem'), 32) is the X-Wing decapsulation key reports seal to, sign_seed = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = m, salt = empty, info = utf8('veyq/v1/moderation/sign'), 32) the Ed25519 key of the key proof. The public bundle is (kem_public, sign_public). kem_seed, sign_seed and sign_public were generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography); kem_public is X-Wing's GenerateKeyPairDerand(kem_seed), which #xwing holds to the draft's published vectors, computed by @noble/post-quantum because no second X-Wing implementation was on hand. The grant of an epoch is seal.asym['moderation-grant'].

moderation_proof.note: ADR 0099 § 2: the key proof every key-proved moderation call carries. statement = lp(utf8('moderation-proof')) || lp(challenge) || lp(utf8(operationId)) || lp(utf8(caseId) or empty) -- the typed statement encoding, the challenge the 32 bytes the server issued, the operationId the contract's, the caseId a canonical lowercase UUID or absent (the empty field). signature = Ed25519(#moderation_key.sign_seed, statement), deterministic. Generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography Ed25519). Asserted by packages/crypto AND by the backend (ModerationProofTest), which rebuilds the statement from the operation it matched.

report_bundle.note: ADR 0093 §§ 1-2, 11: the three plaintexts of a report. keys (a report share's plaintext) = u32be(n) || (lp(utf8(role)) || lp(utf8(ref) or empty) || lp(key))... with 1 <= n <= 256, a role ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,15}$, ref a canonical lowercase UUID or absent, key 32 bytes. body (the moderation-report seal's plaintext) = lp(K_report) || lp(utf8(reason)) || lp(utf8(context)), the texts NFC, zero-padded to the next multiple of 512 bytes. contact (the moderation-report-contact seal's plaintext, present only when the reporter left one) = lp(utf8(contact)), NFC, not blank, at most 254 bytes, zero-padded to 512 bytes — sealed apart from the body so the server can drop it alone six months after the decision was told (ADR 0093 § 11) while the body stays with its case. Generated by an independent Python implementation of this layout; the reason here is written decomposed (u + U+0308) and encoded composed, which pins the NFC step.

body.reason: Grüße — this picture shows a threat.

identity_pin.note: ADR 0104: the identity-pin store as one sealed entry per pin under a sealed head. k_pin_index = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = master_key, salt = empty, info = "veyq/v1/identity-pin-index", 32); pinId = HMAC-SHA256(k_pin_index, utf8(userId)), the 32 bytes an entry is stored and sealed at (seal.sym.identity-pin, [pinId] as a digest field) and carried on the wire as 64 lowercase hex characters. An entry's plaintext is the compact UTF-8 JSON {u: userId, f: fingerprint, h: head, i: index, t: firstSeenAt, r: replaced} in that key order (single-letter keys, so an entry with its head stays inside entry_bytes, ADR 0028 Decision 2), f being b64std of the contact's 32-byte fingerprint hash (#fingerprint's hash) and i the index of that head's step in its chain (-1 for a head pinned unread, at an invite's accept), r 1 when a join record replaced a pin that was not on its chain (ADR 0111 decision 15) and else 0, h b64std of the contact's key-chain head (#key_chain; synthetic here: sha256('veyq/v1/key-chain/head' || utf8(userId))), padded with spaces (0x20) to exactly entry_bytes, so every entry seals to one length. The set digest = SHA-256(utf8("veyq/v1/identity-pin-set") || lp(pinId) || lp(SHA-256(entry)) ...) over the entries in ascending pinId byte order, entry being the sealed entry's decoded bytes; never an incremental digest (ADR 0104 decision 4). The head (seal.sym.identity-pins, bound to its revision) carries compact JSON {version: 2, count, digest: b64std(set digest)}; seal.sym.identity-pins' plaintext is set.empty's head, and seal.sym.identity-pin is pin_ids[0]'s entry, the first of set.two (listed opposite to pinId order, so the canonical sort is load-bearing). Generated by an independent Python implementation (hashlib/hmac + cryptography HKDF and AES-GCM). Asserted by packages/crypto only: the server holds no master key.

invite_key.note: ADR 0111 decisions 1-2: an invite key is an identity-shaped bundle derived from a 32-byte seed. kem_seed = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = seed, salt = empty, info = utf8('veyq/v1/invite/kem'), 32) is its X-Wing decapsulation key, sign_seed = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = seed, salt = empty, info = utf8('veyq/v1/invite/sign'), 32) its Ed25519 key; bundle = lp(kem_public) || lp(sign_public), the serializeIdentityPublic form a grant is sealed to and the wire carries. The owner signs it (decision 1): statement = lp(utf8('invite-key')) || lp(utf8(tenantId)) || lp(utf8(inviteId)) || lp(sha256(bundle)) || lp(u64be(expiresAt)), expiresAt in Unix seconds; signature = Ed25519(owner sign seed = #grant_signature.sign_seed, statement). The owner's bundle is lp(#xwing.vectors[0].pk) || lp(owner_sign_public), its fingerprint hash sha256(utf8('veyq/v1/fingerprint') || bundle). kem_seed, sign_seed, sign_public, the statement and both signatures were generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography); kem_public is X-Wing's GenerateKeyPairDerand(kem_seed), computed by @noble/post-quantum because no second X-Wing implementation was on hand. Asserted by packages/crypto only: the server stores the bundle and the signature and checks neither.

invite_link.note: ADR 0111 decision 1 (the seal is mandatory — the operator mails the link): a member invite's link is https://<domain>/tenant/accept#<token>.<sealed>. The code is 10 Crockford base32 characters (0-9, A-Z without I, L, O, U); a typed code is case-folded, stripped of spaces and hyphens, and I/L read as 1, O as 0 (typed -> code). secret = utf8(code) for a code, utf8(NFC(password)) as typed for a password; kek = Argon2id(secret, salt) at the PRODUCTION profile (t=3, m=32 MiB, p=1, 32 bytes) — the link came through the operator's mail, so the client accepts no other. payload (version 2, ADR 0111 decision 19) = 0x02 || lp(seed) || lp(signerHead) || lp(utf8(signerUserId)) with the seed and owner of #invite_key; signerHead (32 bytes) is the head of the owner's key chain when they signed, here the head of its step 0: signer_genesis = lp(utf8('key-chain-genesis')) || lp(utf8(owner user_id)) || lp(owner bundle) || lp(#secret_key_proof.key.public_key), signer_head = sha256(utf8('veyq/v1/key-chain/head') || signer_genesis) (#key_chain). A payload of any other version is refused; payload_v1 is the retired layout lp(seed) || lp(signerFingerprintHash) || lp(utf8(signerUserId)), kept as the refusal's input; it is sealed as seal.sym['invite-link'] (context_bytes below) under kek_code with nonce: blob = 0x02 || nonce || AES-256-GCM(kek, nonce, payload, 0x02 || 'v1' || context_bytes). sealed = base64url-unpadded(mode || kdfParams || blob), mode 0x01 = code, 0x02 = password, kdfParams = u32be(t) || u32be(m) || u32be(p) || u32be(dkLen) || salt (#kdf_params). fragment = token '.' sealed. Generated by an independent Python implementation (cryptography Argon2id + AESGCM, hashlib), which first re-derived the version-1 blob and sealed part byte for byte.

join_record.note: ADR 0111 decisions 3 and 12: the newcomer's join record and the invite key's accept proof. The joiner's identity bundle is lp(kem_public) || lp(Ed25519 public of joiner_sign_seed); the Secret-Key proof public key is #secret_key_proof.key.public_key; the invite and owner are #invite_key's. statement = lp(utf8('join-record')) || lp(utf8(tenantId)) || lp(utf8(userId)) || lp(sha256(identity bundle)) || lp(secretKeyProofPublicKey) || lp(utf8(inviteId)) || lp(sha256(invite bundle)) || lp(inviteKeySignature) || lp(u64be(inviteExpiresAt)) || lp(utf8(signerUserId)) || lp(sha256(signer bundle)); invite_signature = Ed25519(#invite_key.sign_seed, statement), identity_signature = Ed25519(joiner_sign_seed, statement). record = 0x01 || lp(identity bundle) || lp(proof key) || lp(utf8(inviteId)) || lp(invite bundle) || lp(inviteKeySignature) || lp(u64be(inviteExpiresAt)) || lp(utf8(signerUserId)) || lp(signer bundle) || lp(invite_signature) || lp(identity_signature) — the plaintext sealed as field_seal['member-join-record'] bound to (tenant, userId). accept_statement = lp(utf8('invite-accept')) || lp(utf8(inviteId)) || lp(utf8(userId)) || lp(sha256(identity bundle)); accept_signature = Ed25519(#invite_key.sign_seed, accept_statement). The joiner's kem_public was computed by @noble/post-quantum (no second X-Wing implementation on hand); everything else by an independent Python implementation (cryptography Ed25519). The accept proof is asserted by packages/crypto AND by the backend (InviteAcceptProofTest), which verifies it under the stored invite bundle before it writes the membership.

join_endorsement.note: ADR 0111 / ADR 0111 decision 21: an owner's endorsement of a member's join record they rooted. statement = lp(utf8('join-endorsement')) || lp(utf8(tenantId)) || lp(utf8(userId)) || lp(utf8(signerUserId)) || lp(recordDigest), recordDigest = sha256(the member's OPENED join record — the plaintext a reader opens from sealedJoinRecord, ADR 0115 decision 8, so a rotation's re-seal of the envelope keeps the endorsement); the digest's input is opaque bytes to the statement, and this vector feeds it sealed_join_record (field_seal['member-join-record']'s envelope, named for when the envelope was signed — the statement, its digest and the signature are those bytes' either way); signature = Ed25519(owner sign seed = #grant_signature.sign_seed, statement), the owner being #invite_key.owner (sign_public, bundle). Bound to the record, not its envelope: it endorses that one record, the reader checks the digest against the record it opens, and the server, which opens nothing, checks the signature over the digest the client names. Generated by an independent Python implementation (hashlib + cryptography Ed25519). Asserted by packages/crypto AND by the backend (JoinEndorsementTest), which verifies a staged endorsement under the stage's identity over the record digest the stage names.

key_chain.note: ADR 0111 decision 7, cr-secure-the-account: an account's key chain. Step 0 = the typed statement 'key-chain-genesis': lp(utf8('key-chain-genesis')) || lp(utf8(userId)) || lp(identity bundle) || lp(secretKeyProofPublicKey), unsigned. Step i >= 1 = 'key-chain-step': lp(utf8('key-chain-step')) || lp(utf8(userId)) || lp(u64be(i)) || lp(previousHead) || lp(sha256(retired identity bundle)) || lp(sha256(retired proof public key)) || lp(new identity bundle) || lp(new proof public key), signed over those bytes by the retired identity's Ed25519 key (identity_signature) AND by the retired Secret-Key proof key (proof_signature). head = sha256(utf8('veyq/v1/key-chain/head') || statement) of a step; previousHead of step i is step i-1's head. An identity bundle is lp(kem) || lp(Ed25519 public of sign_seeds[i]); the kem halves are fixed 1216-byte fills (the chain signs bundle bytes and never encapsulates, so key validity is irrelevant, as in #fingerprint). Proof keys from secret_keys[i] as #secret_key_proof.key derives them. failures: each replaces links[2] and names the reason verifyKeyChain refuses it with, at step 2 (wrong_predecessor's signatures are genuine, over the statement naming step 0's head). Generated by an independent Python implementation (hashlib + cryptography Ed25519/HKDF). Asserted by packages/crypto and by the backend, which checks a published step under the stored identity and proof key.

verification.note: ADR 0111 decisions 12-13: a member's verification of another member in one tenant. statement = lp(utf8('verification')) || lp(utf8(tenantId)) || lp(utf8(verifierUserId)) || lp(utf8(subjectUserId)) || lp(subjectHead) || lp(verifierHead), each head a 32-byte key-chain head (#key_chain: subject_head is links[1].head of that chain's user, verifier_head synthetic as links[0].head); signature = Ed25519(sign_seed, statement) by the verifier's identity. record = 0x01 || lp(subjectHead) || lp(verifierHead) || lp(signature), fixed sizes 32/32/64 - the plaintext sealed as field_seal['member-verification'] bound to (tenant, verifier, subject, epoch). It counts while subjectHead is the subject's current head and the signature verifies under the verifier's current identity with verifierHead its current head; a rotation re-signs (decision 13). Generated by an independent Python implementation (hashlib + cryptography Ed25519). Asserted by packages/crypto only: the server never opens one.

rotation_stage.note: ADR 0111 decision 6: the digest the publish binds its staged self-grants by. digest = sha256(utf8('veyq/v1/rotation-stage') || lp(utf8(scopeId)) || lp(u64be(epoch)) || lp(sha256(wrappedGrant)) ...) over the entries in ascending scopeId byte order (canonical lowercase UUIDs), one per scope; wrappedGrant DECODED. entries are listed opposite to that order, so the canonical sort is load-bearing; empty is the digest of no entry. Generated by an independent Python implementation (hashlib). Asserted by packages/crypto and by the backend, which recomputes it over the staged rows.

scope_succession.note: ADR 0115 decision 5: a scope key is replaced at each rotation, never chained, and the new one is proven by a succession statement. Each epoch's key K derives succession_seed = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = K, salt = empty, info = utf8('veyq/v1/scope-succession'), 32), an Ed25519 seed, and from it the epoch's succession public key. statement = lp(utf8('scope-succession')) || lp(utf8(scopeId)) || lp(u64be(epoch)) || lp(successionPublicKey) -- the typed statement encoding, epoch the NEW epoch, successionPublicKey that epoch's 32-byte public key; signature = Ed25519(the previous epoch's succession_seed, statement), deterministic. Here scope_key is epoch 4's key and next_scope_key epoch 5's, and the statement proves epoch 5 from epoch 4. Generated by an independent Python implementation (struct + cryptography HKDF/Ed25519). Asserted by packages/crypto.
